TA-led tutorials. Each entry says what you do in it, which lecture or assignment it supports, and where to find its
materials.

## Block 2 {#block-2}

### B2T1: Cluster/EMR {#emr-cluster}

- **What you do:** You launch an EMR cluster from the AWS console in your sandbox account, step by step, and check
  that it starts. You then terminate the cluster so that it stops billing.
- **Supports:** L5 (Spark on a cluster) and A2, which runs its Spark job on EMR at two and then four core nodes.
- **Materials:** step-by-step guide on Canvas.

### B2T2: Spark/Glue {#glue-tutorial}

Two parts, each a Glue notebook in the [B2T2 repository](https://github.com/cpsc436c-2026w1/l7-spark-glue).
Set up your account once with the repository's
[step 1](https://github.com/cpsc436c-2026w1/l7-spark-glue#1-set-up-your-account-once) before part A.

A Glue session bills until it stops, even after you close the browser tab. End each notebook with its last cell,
`%stop_session`.

#### Part A: how Spark reads files {#glue-part-a}

- **What you do:** You run the notebook in your sandbox account and see, for each query, which folders, files and row
  groups Spark reads and how many tasks it starts. Exercises 2 to 6 then ask you to predict those numbers for new
  queries on the 36 months of taxi trips.
- **Supports:** L7 (Spark as a managed service, and its demos on reading files).
- **Materials:** the notebook [`l7a_data-read.ipynb`](https://github.com/cpsc436c-2026w1/l7-spark-glue/blob/main/l7a_data-read.ipynb).

#### Part B: slow queries and their fixes {#glue-part-b}

- **What you do:** You run three slow queries from L6 on Glue: input that can't be split finely enough, a join on a
  hot key and a window query. Before each run you write down how many tasks you expect, then you read the stage
  table to find what makes the query slow and which change fixes it. Exercises B1 to B5 follow, with their answers
  in commented-out cells.
- **Supports:** [L6](w2-l6.qmd) (why a cluster job is slow) and L7.
- **Materials:** the notebook [`l7b_slow-queries.ipynb`](https://github.com/cpsc436c-2026w1/l7-spark-glue/blob/main/l7b_slow-queries.ipynb).

## Block 3 {#block-3}

### B3T1: Lakehouse/Athena+Glue {#b3-t1}

- **What you do:** You query the course's rides table in Athena, predicting how much each query reads before you
  run it. You then copy one month into your own account and change it: delete rows, read the table as it was before
  the delete, load a day twice and repair it, add a column, and join your copy with a course table.
- **Supports:** L10 (lakehouses: Iceberg tables, snapshots and time travel) and L11, and the use and change tasks
  in A3.
- **Before the tutorial:** run the one-time setup in the repository's
  [step 1](https://github.com/cpsc436c-2026w1/b3-t1-athena-rides#1-set-up-your-account-once) (about 8 minutes, in
  CloudShell).
- **Materials:** the [B3T1 repository](https://github.com/cpsc436c-2026w1/b3-t1-athena-rides): the steps, one
  SQL file per step with the expected results, and the setup script.
